siegrist2022_bayesian_set_estimation.title: Probability, Mathematical Statistics, and Stochastic Processes, §8.5: Bayesian Set Estimation

article_lead.description: rules for selecting sets with a specified posterior probability so uncertainty can be reported consistently

new_bank_questions.title: A highest-posterior-probability set on a grid
new_bank_questions.body: A parameter can take values 1, 2 and 3 with posterior probabilities 0.50, 0.30 and 0.20. Give a smallest set with posterior probability at least 80%, choosing the most probable points first. Why does a continuous-density threshold formula need care here?
new_bank_questions.answer: The set {1,2} has posterior probability 0.50+0.30=0.80 and uses two points; no one-point set reaches 0.80. In a discrete distribution probability arrives in jumps, so an exact target may be unattainable at some levels and a threshold may include tied points. Specify at-least content and a rule for ties or excess mass.
